data.name: Aadam
data.gender_notes: Aadam is used as a male name in islamic naming traditions.
data.short_meaning: Man; human being; of the earth (the name of the first prophet, Adam)
data.long_meaning: Arabic Ādam (آدم), the name of the first human being and first prophet in Islamic tradition. The name is cognate with Hebrew ʾādām 'man, human', and is traditionally connected with the sense 'made of earth / clay'. It is not a descriptive Arabic word in ordinary use but a proper name. Aadam therefore means “Man; human being; of the earth (the name of the first prophet, Adam)”. Qur'anic prophet name; Ādam is named in the Qur'an (e.g. 2:31, 7:19) as the first human and first prophet.
data.spiritual_meaning: Aadam expresses “First man created by Allah”; spiritual readings of the name are interpretive.

faq.q: Is Aadam mentioned in the Qur'an?
faq.a: Yes. Ādam (آدم) is named in the Qur'an as the first human being and the first prophet, for example in Surah al-Baqarah (2:31) and Surah al-A'raf (7:19).

faq.q: What does the name Aadam mean?
faq.a: Aadam means “Man; human being; of the earth (the name of the first prophet, Adam)”.

faq.q: Where does the name Aadam come from?
What is the linguistic root of Aadam?
faq.a: The root of Aadam is آدم (ʾādam), related to Hebrew אָדָם.

faq.q: How is Aadam written in Arabic script?
faq.a: Aadam is written آدم in Arabic script.

faq.q: Is Aadam a boy's or a girl's name?
faq.a: Aadam is used as a male name.

faq.q: Is Aadam mentioned in the Qur'an?
faq.a: Ādam is named in the Qur'an as the first human being and first prophet.

faq.q: Is the meaning of Aadam verified?
faq.a: Yes — the meaning “Man; human being; of the earth (the name of the first prophet, Adam)” is established by Qur'anic prophet name; Ādam is named in the Qur'an (e.g. 2:31, 7:19) as the first human and first prophet..
